subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Chan Chan: The Largest Adobe City
description: A fast breakdown of Chan Chan: The Largest Adobe City for builders.

hook.text: The largest mud-brick city ever built is slowly dissolving in the rain on Peru's northern coast.

buildup.text: Chan Chan was the capital of the Chimú Empire, covering eight square miles and housing 60,000 people by 1400 CE.

discovery.text: Its walls are covered in intricate friezes of fish, birds, and waves — all carved into dried mud.

twist.text: The Inca conquered the Chimú in 1470 by diverting their water supply. No battle was needed — just thirst.

climax.text: El Niño rains are eroding the city faster each decade. Climate change may destroy what the Inca could not.

punchline.text: An empire fell to thirst. Its capital is falling to rain.

quiz.question: How did the Inca conquer the Chimú at Chan Chan?
options: They laid siege for three years until food ran out
They diverted the city's water supply, defeating them with thirst
They used superior bronze weapons to overwhelm mud-brick walls
